answer: Each identity posts a claim to a lantern ledger and locks a 60-credit bond. The claim links to its prior work through a vine thread, so a copy breaks the thread. Five summit reviewers must co-sign it, each staking 20 credits. Auditors recompute the lantern record; a fake burns 60 plus 100 credits. The k-th fake pays 158 plus 2 times k, as reviewer capacity is three per epoch. The 1,000th fake costs 2,158; 1,000 fakes cost 1,159,000. Rented reviewers fail: the ledger exposes heavy signers and burns their stakes. An honest identity locks one bond and gets it back after one quorum.
